action_summary: The capability matrix was counting one case as two and two cases as one fixture. ``build()`` names its fixture directory after the case and rmtree's it before writing, and ``measure_coverage`` is registered twice -- once in the toolchain lane over ``pkg``, once in the analysis lane over ``cov/calc.py``. So the two cases shared one directory and destroyed each other's tree mid-run: measured on 56f43613, the REAL list printed ``measure_coverage`` twice (54 cases, 53 distinct names) and the headline count moved between 42 and 44 across runs on an unchanged tree. The directory is now keyed on registration index, so it is unique whatever the label is; measured after the change, three consecutive runs give 44 REAL / 0 FALSE / 0 DAMAGED with all 54 directories distinct. The document that reports these numbers was regenerated in the same commit: it now reads its commit from git instead of a hand-typed string, reads every per-class failure off the requests that actually failed, counts cases rather than names, and prints a floor over several runs instead of one sample.

recursive_obs.stop_condition: STOP when no two cases can share a fixture directory, when the REAL count equals the number of distinct cases and does not move on an unchanged tree, and when the published inventory's commit, class table and defect table are all read from measurement rather than typed.
recursive_obs.why_selected_route_is_fastest_sufficient: The adapter already performs this extraction correctly -- called with qualname=total and lines 3-4 it returns gate PASS and one edit -- so the refusal was never a missing capability. The derivation module already had a block that computes a span from a host function's statements; it was unreachable because the binder wrote a 0 first and because the host phrase pattern only knew 'in <name>'. Two rules reuse both, no new module, and the alternative -- teaching the adapter to guess a region -- would have made the door invent what the sentence did not say.
